deploy-bot: DeployBot started a config-only canary for route /v1/generate. Change set: tenant_conn_cap: 6 -> 4, default_timeout_ms: 2200 -> 3000, route_weight: 0.05 -> 0.10. Canary slice: 1% traffic for 15m. cfg-id: cfg-2026-03-21-01

mira: ACK. thanks. can we confirm dashboards are warming (latency, errors, kvcache)?

jasper: dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/abc123/canary-overview (latency + kvcache panel). looking now.

sam: smoke test queued: `curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'` -> expect 200 and reasonable latency.

deploy-bot: [INFO] canary ramp to 1% at 2026-03-21T18:22:17Z

lee: saw 95p latency +30ms at t+3m on the canary slice, no error increase yet. attaching short log snippet.

sam: paste logs — couple of allocation spikes for tenant=acme-prod around the same time: ```
2026-03-21T18:25:11Z tenant=acme-prod runtime: allocation failed: out of memory
2026-03-21T18:25:12Z tenant=acme-prod inference: evicting kv entries
```

jasper: batching avg size dropped ~12% on the canary. reduced batch = higher per-token overhead. dropping conn cap might be making some tenants send more concurrent smaller requests.

mira: okay — plan suggestion: hold the ramp, reduce global canary slice to 0.5% and apply a targeted pin for acme-prod to previous conn cap (6) while we investigate. keep route_weight at 0.05 for safety.

deploy-bot: [ACTION] executing partial rollback: set global route_weight -> 0.05, canary slice -> 0.5%, and create tenant override: acme-prod.tenant_conn_cap=6 (pinned). will report completion.

deploy-bot: [INFO] partial rollback applied at 2026-03-21T18:28:45Z (cfg-id rollback: cfg-2026-03-21-01-revert-acme)

sam: re-running acme smoke now. `curl` results: 200 OK, p95 back to baseline (within noise).

lee: monitoring: kvcache hit rate steady, batching avg recovering. no new OOMs in the last 3m.

jasper: marking this canary as HOLD for followup (need a root cause on why smaller batches + lower conn cap exposed acme). I'll open a short postmortem with traces.

mira: good. add a note to the release notes: "config-only: attempted conn_cap decrease + timeout bump; partial rollback applied for acme-prod due to transient allocation spikes; global route_weight restored to previous value." I'll keep this thread open for 20m then close if stable. :memo:

lee: :thumbsup:

sam: thanks folks — will follow up in the postmortem with heap profiles.

deploy-bot: [CLOSED?] will auto-close thread after 20m of no activity.
